complications.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
complications.source_text: There is an increasing appreciation of the common pathophysiology and interrelationship of cardiometabolic risk factors leading to both adverse cardiovascular and adverse kidney outcomes in people with diabetes, including ASCVD, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) (17,18).

complications.name: Heart Failure
complications.source_text: CVD also includes heart failure, and diabetes is a risk factor for incident heart failure, which is at least twofold more prevalent in people with diabetes compared with those without diabetes and is a major cause of morbidity and mortality (11).

complications.name: Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease
complications.source_text: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a broad term that includes atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and heart failure, two CVDs common among people with diabetes.

complications.name: Hypertension
complications.source_text: Hypertension is common among people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Hypertension is a major risk factor for ASCVD, heart failure, and microvascular complications.

complications.name: Microvascular Complications
complications.source_text: Hypertension is a major risk factor for ASCVD, heart failure, and microvascular complications.

complications.name: Autonomic Neuropathy
complications.source_text: Postural changes in blood pressure and pulse may be evidence of autonomic neuropathy and therefore require adjustment of blood pressure goals.

complications.name: Acute Kidney Injury
complications.source_text: Treatment with ACE inhibitors and ARBs or MRAs can cause AKI and hyperkalemia, while diuretics can cause AKI and either hypokalemia or hyperkalemia (depending on mechanism of action) (77,78).

complications.name: Hyperkalemia
complications.source_text: Treatment with ACE inhibitors and ARBs or MRAs can cause AKI and hyperkalemia, while diuretics can cause AKI and either hypokalemia or hyperkalemia (depending on mechanism of action) (77,78).

complications.name: Hypotension
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Syncope
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Bradycardia
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Statin Intolerance
complications.source_text: Statin therapy is a cornerstone of CVD prevention and treatment; however, a subset of individuals experience partial (inability to tolerate sufficient dosage necessary to achieve therapeutic objectives due to adverse effects) or complete (inability to tolerate any dose) intolerance to statin therapy (127).

complications.name: Hypertriglyceridemia
complications.source_text: In adults with hypertriglyceridemia (fasting triglycerides >150 mg/dL [>1.7 mmol/L] or nonfasting triglycerides >175 mg/dL [>2.0 mmol/L]), clinicians should address and treat lifestyle factors (obesity and metabolic syndrome), secondary factors (diabetes, chronic liver or kidney disease and/or nephrotic syndrome, and hypothyroidism), and medications that raise triglycerides. C

complications.name: Low HDL Cholesterol
complications.source_text: Intensify lifestyle therapy and optimize glycemic management for people with diabetes with elevated triglyceride levels (≥150 mg/dL [≥1.7 mmol/L]) and/or low HDL cholesterol (<40 mg/dL [<1.0 mmol/L] for men and <50 mg/dL [<1.3 mmol/L] for women). C

complications.name: Type 2 Diabetes
complications.source_text: Several studies have reported a modestly increased risk of incident type 2 diabetes with statin use (156,157), which may be limited to those with diabetes risk factors and/or impaired glucose tolerance.

complications.name: Bleeding Risk
complications.source_text: Aspirin therapy (75–162 mg/day) may be considered as a primary prevention strategy in those with diabetes who are at increased cardiovascular risk after a comprehensive discussion with the individual on the benefits versus the comparable increased risk of bleeding. A

complications.name: Gastrointestinal Bleeding
complications.source_text: Major bleeding was significantly increased from 3.2 to 4.1% in the aspirin group (rate ratio 1.29; P = 0.003), with most of the excess being gastrointestinal bleeding and other extracranial bleeding.

complications.name: Intracranial Hemorrhage
complications.source_text: Major bleeding was significantly increased from 3.2 to 4.1% in the aspirin group (rate ratio 1.29; P = 0.003), with most of the excess being gastrointestinal bleeding and other extracranial bleeding.

complications.name: Reye Syndrome
complications.source_text: Aspirin use in individuals aged <21 years is generally contraindicated due to the associated risk of Reye syndrome.

complications.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
complications.source_text: Diabetic ketoacidosis and euglycemic ketoacidosis (266).

complications.name: Euglycemic Ketoacidosis
complications.source_text: Diabetic ketoacidosis and euglycemic ketoacidosis (266).

complications.name: Obesity
complications.source_text: Comorbid conditions including overweight and obesity and hypertension often precede the development of HFpEF and have been implicated in the pathophysiology of HFpEF (14).

complications.name: Overweight

screening_tests.name: Blood Pressure Measurement
screening_tests.source_text: Blood pressure should be measured at every routine clinical visit, or at least every 6 months by a trained individual who should follow the guidelines established for the general population: measurement in the seated position, with feet on the floor and arm supported at heart level, after 5 min of rest. Cuff size should be appropriate for the upper-arm circumference (29).
screening_tests.frequency: Every routine clinical visit, or at least every 6 months

screening_tests.name: Home Blood Pressure Self-Monitoring
screening_tests.source_text: Home blood pressure self-monitoring and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring may provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure (30,31).
screening_tests.indication: Confirming or refuting a diagnosis of hypertension, monitoring antihypertensive treatment

screening_tests.name: 24-h Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring
screening_tests.source_text: Home blood pressure self-monitoring and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring may provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure (30,31).
screening_tests.indication: Confirming or refuting a diagnosis of hypertension, monitoring antihypertensive treatment

screening_tests.name: Lipid Profile
screening_tests.source_text: In adults with prediabetes or diabetes not taking statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, it is reasonable to obtain a lipid profile at the time of diagnosis, at an initial medical evaluation, annually thereafter, or more frequently if indicated. E
screening_tests.frequency: At diagnosis, initial medical evaluation, annually thereafter, or more frequently if indicated
screening_tests.indication: Adults with prediabetes or diabetes not taking statins or other lipid-lowering therapy

screening_tests.name: Lipid Panel
screening_tests.source_text: Obtain a lipid profile at initiation of statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, 4–12 weeks after initiation or a change in dose, and annually thereafter, as it facilitates monitoring the response to therapy and informs medication-taking behavior. A
screening_tests.frequency: At initiation of statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, 4–12 weeks after initiation or a change in dose, and annually thereafter
screening_tests.indication: Monitoring response to statins or other lipid-lowering therapy

screening_tests.name: Ankle-Brachial Index Testing
screening_tests.source_text: In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, screening for PAD with ankle-brachial index testing is recommended if a PAD diagnosis would change management. B
screening_tests.indication: Screening for PAD in asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, if a PAD diagnosis would change management

screening_tests.name: Natriuretic Peptide Measurement
screening_tests.source_text: Consider screening adults with diabetes by measuring a natriuretic peptide (B-type natriuretic peptide [BNP] or N-terminal pro-BNP [NT-proBNP]) to facilitate prevention of stage C heart failure.
screening_tests.indication: Screening adults with diabetes to facilitate prevention of stage C heart failure

screening_tests.name: Echocardiography
screening_tests.source_text: In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and abnormal natriuretic peptide levels, echocardiography is recommended to identify stage B heart failure. A
screening_tests.indication: Asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and abnormal natriuretic peptide levels to identify stage B heart failure

screening_tests.name: Coronary Artery Calcium Measurement
screening_tests.source_text: In adults with diabetes ≥40 years of age, measurement of coronary artery calcium is also reasonable for cardiovascular risk assessment.
screening_tests.indication: Cardiovascular risk assessment in adults with diabetes ≥40 years of age

screening_tests.name: Pharmacologic Stress Echocardiography
screening_tests.source_text: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography or nuclear imaging should be considered in individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing (e.g., left bundle branch block or ST-T abnormalities).
screening_tests.indication: Individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing

screening_tests.name: Nuclear Imaging
screening_tests.source_text: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography or nuclear imaging should be considered in individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing (e.g., left bundle branch block or ST-T abnormalities).
screening_tests.indication: Individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing

therapeutic_agents.name: ACE Inhibitor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: An ACE inhibitor (ACEi) or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) is suggested for the treatment of hypertension in people with coronary artery disease (CAD) or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 30–299 mg/g creatinine and is strongly recommended for individuals with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥300 mg/g creatinine.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Hypertension in people with coronary artery disease (CAD) or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 30–299 mg/g creatinine; strongly recommended for individuals with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥300 mg/g creatinine.

therapeutic_agents.name: Angiotensin Receptor Blocker
therapeutic_agents.source_text: An ACE inhibitor (ACEi) or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) is suggested for the treatment of hypertension in people with coronary artery disease (CAD) or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 30–299 mg/g creatinine and is strongly recommended for individuals with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥300 mg/g creatinine.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Hypertension in people with coronary artery disease (CAD) or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 30–299 mg/g creatinine; strongly recommended for individuals with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥300 mg/g creatinine.

therapeutic_agents.name: Calcium Channel Blocker
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Start two drugs from ACEi or ARB, CCB† or diuretic‡
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Hypertension, when starting two drugs

therapeutic_agents.name: Diuretic
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Start two drugs from ACEi or ARB, CCB† or diuretic‡

therapeutic_agents.name: Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Consider addition of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; refer to specialist with expertise in BP management
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Resistant hypertension, not meeting goal or adverse effects using a drug from each of three classes

therapeutic_agents.name: Sodium–Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: treatment with SGLT inhibitors and/or GLP-1 RAs that have demonstrated cardiovascular and kidney benefit is considered a fundamental element of risk reduction and a core pharmacological strategy to improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes (Fig. 10.1).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Fundamental element of risk reduction and a core pharmacological strategy to improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes

therapeutic_agents.name: Statin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: For people with diabetes aged 40–75 years without ASCVD, use moderate-intensity statin therapy in addition to lifestyle therapy. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Primary prevention in people with diabetes aged 40–75 years without ASCVD

therapeutic_agents.name: Bempedoic Acid
therapeutic_agents.source_text: In people with diabetes intolerant to statin therapy, treatment with bempedoic acid is recommended to reduce cardiovascular event rates as an alternative cholesterol-lowering plan. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Alternative cholesterol-lowering plan in people with diabetes intolerant to statin therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: Ezetimibe
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The addition of ezetimibe or a PCSK9 inhibitor is recommended if this goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: If LDL cholesterol goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: PCSK9 Inhibitor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The addition of ezetimibe or a PCSK9 inhibitor is recommended if this goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: If LDL cholesterol goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: Icosapent Ethyl
therapeutic_agents.source_text: In individuals with ASCVD or other cardiovascular risk factors on a statin with managed LDL cholesterol but elevated triglycerides (150–499 mg/dL [1.7–5.6 mmol/L]), the addition of icosapent ethyl can be considered to reduce cardiovascular risk. B
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Individuals with ASCVD or other cardiovascular risk factors on a statin with managed LDL cholesterol but elevated triglycerides (150–499 mg/dL [1.7–5.6 mmol/L])

therapeutic_agents.name: Aspirin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Use aspirin therapy (75–162 mg/day) as a secondary prevention strategy in those with diabetes and a history of ASCVD. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Secondary prevention in those with diabetes and a history of ASCVD

therapeutic_agents.name: Clopidogrel
therapeutic_agents.source_text: For individuals with ASCVD and documented aspirin allergy, clopidogrel (75 mg/day) should be used. B
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Individuals with ASCVD and documented aspirin allergy

therapeutic_agents.name: Rivaroxaban
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Combination therapy with 81 mg aspirin daily plus 2.5 mg rivaroxaban twice daily should be considered for individuals with stable coronary and/or peripheral artery disease (PAD) and low bleeding risk to prevent major adverse limb and cardiovascular events. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Individuals with stable coronary and/or peripheral artery disease (PAD) and low bleeding risk

therapeutic_agents.name: Finerenone
therapeutic_agents.source_text: People with type 2 diabetes and CKD should be considered for treatment with finerenone to reduce cardiovascular outcomes and the risk of CKD progression (239–242).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: People with type 2 diabetes and CKD to reduce cardiovascular outcomes and the risk of CKD progression

therapeutic_agents.name: Empagliflozin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Results of large cardiovascular outcome trials of empagliflozin (10 mg or 25 mg daily) and canagliflozin (100 or 300 mg daily) showed that treatment with either drug reduced rates of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To reduce rates of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death

therapeutic_agents.name: Canagliflozin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Results of large cardiovascular outcome trials of empagliflozin (10 mg or 25 mg daily) and canagliflozin (100 or 300 mg daily) showed that treatment with either drug reduced rates of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To reduce rates of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death

therapeutic_agents.name: Dapagliflozin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The major cardiovascular outcome trial of dapagliflozin (10 mg daily) did not show a reduction in the coprimary outcome of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death but did show a significantly lower rate of the co-primary composite outcome of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death, which was driven by its effect on hospitalization for heart failure.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To reduce hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death

therapeutic_agents.name: Liraglutide
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Results of trials with the GLP-1 RAs liraglutide (once daily) and semaglutide, and dulaglutide.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: As indicated for GLP-1 RA therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: Semaglutide
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Results of trials with the GLP-1 RAs liraglutide (once daily) and semaglutide, and dulaglutide.

therapeutic_agents.name: Tirzepatide
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Cardiovascular outcome trials of the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 RA tirzepatide are ongoing (261).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: As indicated for dual GIP/GLP-1 RA therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: Spironolactone
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Consistent with heart failure guidelines, an MRA like spironolactone or eplerenone is recommended in people with HFrEF (ejection fraction ≤40%) and type 2 diabetes (12,13).
